## Phase 7: Neural-Kernel-Sentinel (`src/security/`)

**Total: 1,508 lines of source + 854 lines of tests = 2,362 lines**

| File | Lines | Role |
|------|-------|------|
| `syscall_interceptor.fl` | 265 | Lock-free ring buffer, 4K capacity, 32 syscall categories |
| `behavioral_analyzer.fl` | 382 | N-gram anomaly detection, 16-dim feature vectors |
| `threat_classifier.fl` | 319 | 3-layer NN (16→32→16→8), 8 threat types, ensemble scoring |
| `response_engine.fl` | 302 | Policy-based response, SIGSTOP/KILL dispatch |
| `mod.fl` | 240 | E2E pipeline, NeuralKernelSentinel struct |

### Key Structs & Enums

- `SyscallEvent { timestamp_ns, syscall_id, category, pid, uid, return_code, arg0-2, duration_ns }`
- `SyscallCategory` - 28 variants (FileRead..RawSocket)
- `SyscallFeatureVector` - 16 dimensions (D0-D4 category rates, D5-D9 N-gram anomaly, D10-D12 timing, D13-D15 privilege)
- `SimpleNN { w1[16x32], b1[32], w2[32x16], b2[16], w3[16x8], b3[8] }`
- `ThreatType` - 8 variants: Normal, ZeroDay, PrivilegeEscalation, CodeInjection, DataExfiltration, PersistenceMechanism, LateralMovement, CoverageEvasion
- `AlertSeverity` - Info / Warning / Critical / Emergency (by confidence threshold)
- `NeuralKernelSentinel { interceptor, analyzer, classifier, response_engine, detection_count, total_latency_us, max_latency_us }`

### Module Reference Chain (Phase 7)
```
syscall_interceptor.fl
    <- behavioral_analyzer.fl    (pub use super::syscall_interceptor::...)
        <- threat_classifier.fl  (pub use super::behavioral_analyzer::...)
            <- response_engine.fl (pub use super::threat_classifier::...)
                <- mod.fl        (integrates all 4 + NeuralKernelSentinel)
```

### Test File Structure
```
tests/neural_kernel_sentinel_test.fl (854 lines)
  Group A: A1-A6  - Syscall Interceptor (ring buffer, bit-mask, 32 categories)
  Group B: B1-B6  - Behavioral Analyzer (N-gram, feature vector, 16 dims)
  Group C: C1-C6  - Threat Classifier (NN forward pass, ensemble weights)
  Group D: D1-D6  - Response Engine (policy, SIGSTOP/KILL latency)
  Group E: E1-E6  - Integration E2E (< 100µs end-to-end pipeline)
```

## Phase 6: ML Online Learning (`src/ml/`)

**Total: 1,556 lines**

| File | Lines | Role |
|------|-------|------|
| `gradient_descent.fl` | 436 | SGDOptimizer, NeuralNetworkWeights, forward/backward pass |
| `online_learning_pipeline.fl` | 401 | Real-time batch update, VecDeque buffer |
| `model_evaluation.fl` | 437 | PerformanceMetrics, DriftDetectionResult (KL divergence) |
| `mod.fl` | 282 | MLOnlineLearningSystem, ThreatSample, integration API |

### Key Structs (Phase 6)

- `SGDOptimizer { learning_rate, momentum: 0.9, decay: 0.001, batch_size: 32, velocity: Vec<f64>[1208] }`
- `NeuralNetworkWeights` - full 3-layer weight store
- `TrainingSample { features: Vec<f64>[16], label: u32[0-7], confidence: f64, timestamp_ns }`
- `OnlineLearningPipeline { sgd, weights, batch_buffer: VecDeque, update_interval_ms, samples_seen, total_loss_history }`
- `PerformanceMetrics { precision, recall, f1_score, accuracy, auc_roc }`
- `DriftDetectionResult` - KL divergence drift (threshold < 0.2)
- `ThreatSample` - bridge between ML pipeline and NKS threat types

### Phase 6 → Phase 7 Connection
The ML module feeds learned weights into Phase 7's `SimpleNN`. The `ThreatSample` in `ml/mod.fl` directly maps `ThreatType` from `security/threat_classifier.fl`. Phase 6 updates weights online; Phase 7 uses them for real-time < 100µs inference.
